rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls a prayer without Umm al-Qurʾān deficient and incomplete; when asked about praying behind an imam, Abu Hurayra tells them to recite it quietly.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In the divine report, Allah says the central declaration of worship and request for help belongs jointly to Him and the servant, who receives what he asks.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

words: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: When the servant asks for the guided path and names those favored rather than those under anger or astray, Allah says this request is for the servant and grants what was asked.
rows.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم * صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet’s prayer instructions: keep the rows straight, follow the imam’s takbīr, bowing, and prostration after him, and recite the sitting testimony.
rows.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبنا فبين لنا سنتنا وعلمنا صلاتنا فقال

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa says the Prophet taught worshippers to answer the recitation’s ending with Amin, so that God answers them; the teaching arose after a man spoke during prayer.
rows.anchor: عن حطان بن عبد الله الرقاشي قال صليت مع أبي موسى الأشعري صلاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet promises forgiveness of previous sins when the reciter and those behind him say Amin in unison with the heavenly utterance.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that believers feared they could not bear accountability for hidden thoughts in 2:284; the Prophet told them to affirm hearing and obeying rather than answer as earlier scriptural communities did.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: After the companions accepted the instruction, their tongues readily recited the words of submission, and the passage beginning “The Messenger believes” was revealed in their wake.
rows.anchor: ذلت بها ألسنتهم فأنزل الله في إثرها

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In Abu Hurayra’s account, Allah answers yes to the petitions in 2:286: pardon for forgetfulness and error, relief from burdens and incapacity, forgiveness, mercy, and aid.
rows.anchor: ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا‏}‏ قال نعم

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The report explicitly says Allah abrogated the earlier passage about accounting for inner thoughts and then revealed the assurance that He burdens no soul beyond its capacity.
rows.anchor: فلما فعلوا ذلك نسخها الله تعالى

words: وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning about hidden thoughts deeply troubled the believers; the Prophet told them to hear, obey, and submit, and Allah placed faith in their hearts before revealing 2:286.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ خَطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: Allah answers “I have done so” to the believers’ prayers for protection from error and burdens, and for forgiveness, mercy, and His guardianship.
rows.anchor: ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jarir reports that the Prophet recited 4:1 and 59:18 while urging a destitute group to give charity, even a half-date; an Anṣārī’s large gift prompted others to contribute food and clothing.
rows.anchor: عن المنذر بن جرير، عن أبيه، قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صدر النهار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever begins a good practice in Islam receives its reward and the reward of followers without diminishing theirs; whoever begins an evil practice bears its burden and theirs.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet barred entering the punished people of al-Hijr except while weeping, lest visitors suffer the same punishment; the report does not discuss 4:23’s marriage prohibitions.
rows.anchor: سمع عبد الله، بن عمر يقول قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحاب الحجر

none: The phrase بني آدم is only a coincidental match to 7:172; this report concerns speech during prayer, divination, and emancipation, not the primordial covenant.
بني آدم is a coincidental wording match; the report about 360 joints and daily charity does not address the covenant in 7:172.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit; he paused for revelation, then answered that the spirit is by God’s command and human knowledge is slight.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال بينما أنا أمشي، مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث وهو متكئ على عسيب إذ مر بنفر من اليهود

words: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim notes a wording difference in this parallel report: Wakiʿ’s transmission has “you were given,” while ʿIsa ibn Yunus’s has “they were given.”
rows.anchor: في حديث وكيع وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

words: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud’s parallel account places the Prophet in a date grove leaning on a palm stalk; it repeats the question about the spirit and the response that knowledge is limited.
rows.anchor: عن مسروق، عن عبد الله، قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في نخل يتوكأ على عسيب

words: مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet later supplied mounts after swearing he could not, attributing their provision to God; he says he will expiate an oath and do the better act when one presents itself.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى، الأشعري قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في رهط من الأشعريين نستحمله

words: مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Musa recounts the Prophet’s oath about supplying camels and teaching that he will do a better act and expiate; he applies this precedent when inviting a man who had sworn off chicken to eat.
rows.anchor: ثم حملتنا أفنسيت يا رسول الله

none: The words كل من coincide lexically with 19:93, but this report concerns end-time idolatry and the removal of believers, not the verse’s statement that all creation comes as servants.
